pos.personaBrief: Sacchi's Milan wanted to dictate the game with the ball and control space without it ('the team must dictate the game in possession'), always five men ahead of the ball; Italy 1994 was more pragmatic but still combination-based.

pro.personaBrief: Build-up started with the defenders carrying the ball (Coaches' Voice), with short and medium passes by Albertini, but transitions were fast and combinations quick after interceptions.

est.personaBrief: Rehearsed shadow football, fixed zones and lines and chains made positions rigid and drilled (FIFA, Spielverlagerung), with only Baggio given license; wingers moved inside and combined centrally.

lar.personaBrief: 4-4-2 with Donadoni/Colombo moving centrally and width supplied by full-backs; Sacchi wanted a player on each wing but 'it can be anyone', so no reliance on classic wingers, and Italy 1994 narrow 4-3 block.

blo.personaBrief: High line, offside as attack, forwards pressing centre-backs, compact 25 m block and pressing in the opponent half (Coaches' Voice, FIFA, Sky).

mar.personaBrief: Pure zonal marking was the core of the system; he argued against man marking and the sweeper (FIFA, Bleacher Report).

pla.personaBrief: He imposed his own system on arrival at Milan ('those who follow him will remain'), drilled the model and played the same way against anyone, only partly adapting at the 1994 World Cup.

res.personaBrief: Wanted to win on merit and dominate ('90 minutes of joy', 'if you don't win dominating, you must improve'); did not accept a defensive play-for-the-draw mentality.

sis.personaBrief: System over stars: five organised players beat ten disorganised ones, everyone in lines and chains, only Baggio granted some freedom; he looked at the head, not the feet.

jog.personaBrief: Wanted intelligent, multi-purpose runners ('thinks fast' about Ancelotti) and an athletic, intense game; technique mattered but within running and pressing demands.

bas.personaBrief: Built Milan with signings from Serie B/C plus stars like Gullit and Van Basten and relied on senior players Baresi, Maldini; not an academy-centred or youth-first coach, though he launched Zola and Del Piero for Italy.

lid.personaBrief: Autocratic manager who demanded the same rules for all, tension with Van Basten and the big players, Baggio crisis; Berlusconi backed him over players.
